documents.title: Responsible Use of Generative AI
documents.summary: Provost page for faculty and researchers that lists the Task Force's values, cautions about data and accountability, and research-publication pointers. It states a default that unauthorized student AI use is cheating but leaves instructors to decide and communicate their own policy.
documents.stance_why: The page tells instructors to 'Communicate your policy on AI tool use' and says students should 'check with their instructor' when the syllabus is silent, which hands the decision to instructors. It does state a default ('using AI tools as a substitute ... is cheating unless instructors say otherwise'), but most of the page is faculty guidance, not a rule for all work.

units.why: Defines generative AI as a system that 'relies on very large data sets to generate content'; a definition that sets what the guidance covers, so P61, informs, general.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is a system that relies on very large data sets

units.why: Says 'the quality of GAI output varies in terms of accuracy and bias', a fact about unreliable output, closest to P31 (verify output). It states a fact, not a duty, so modality is informs.
units.anchor: the quality of GAI output varies in terms of accuracy and bias
units.fit_note: States the fact of variable accuracy and bias but does not tell anyone to verify.

units.why: The Task Force value says the university 'supports the thoughtful application' of GAI to education, research and administration 'when appropriate'; a principle in an institution-level framework, so P56, a permissive stance.
units.anchor: supports the thoughtful application of new technologies, such as generative artificial intelligence (GAI),

units.why: States education 'with human-to human interaction at the core' and that GAI is 'not a substitute'; a guiding principle for the institution, so P56 rather than P32 (it concerns the university's processes, not a student duty).
units.anchor: provide support for but are not a substitute for these processes.
units.fit_note: Also says AI is support, not a substitute for human-centered teaching, close to P32 but at institution level.

units.why: Says GAI use 'should not reduce equitable access' or 'impinge on rights to ... privacy, due process'; an institution-wide principle on equity and rights, so P56 (framework) rather than P51 which is about cost and access to tools.
units.anchor: should not reduce equitable access to a human-centered, effective, and quality educational experience
units.fit_note: Sets equity, academic freedom, privacy and due-process limits on GAI use.

units.why: Tells instructors 'Communicate your policy on AI tool use to your students'; an instruction to state expectations, so P09 (statement in the syllabus), addressed to instructors at course start.
units.anchor: Communicate your policy on AI tool use to your students
units.fit_note: Says to communicate the policy but names no specific place such as the syllabus.

units.why: 'Absent a statement in the syllabus, students are advised to check with their instructor'; this tells students to ask when the rules are not stated, so P10 rather than P06 (the fallback default is the separate next sentence).
units.anchor: Absent a statement in the syllabus, students are advised to check with their instructor

units.why: 'If you permit the use of these tools, please tell students how you want their use documented or disclosed' asks instructors who allow AI to set disclosure rules; closest is P24 (disclosure), addressed to the instructor.
units.anchor: please tell students how you want their use documented or disclosed
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to specify disclosure expectations rather than requiring disclosure itself.

units.why: 'the default is that using AI tools as a substitute for their authentic intellectual and creative work is cheating unless instructors say otherwise' gives the rule when no instructor decision exists, so P06; it is a restrictive default.
units.anchor: using AI tools as a substitute for their authentic intellectual and creative work is cheating

units.why: Warns that entered data 'will become part of the model used to train that tool'; a privacy fact, so P50 (tools store prompts), informs.
units.anchor: will become part of the model used to train that tool in the future.

units.why: 'Don't enter personal information, copyrighted text, images, or video' forbids sharing personal, copyrighted or protected data with AI, so P50, must-not, addressed to faculty readers.
units.anchor: Don’t enter personal information, copyrighted text, images, or video
units.fit_note: Also forbids entering copyrighted material, which touches P52.

units.why: Says Copilot 'protects user data' when logged in with a UMass NetID under the university license; points users to a vetted licensed tool, so P92 (institution-wide approved tool), informs.
units.anchor: protects user data and does not use user data to train models
units.frag_start: about Copilot which protects user data

units.why: Says IT 'provides an evaluation service of AI tools from a security standpoint'; an institutional review of AI tools, so P65, informs.
units.anchor: IT provides an evaluation service of AI tools

units.why: The Task Force offers recommendations on applying GAI 'to traditionally human activities such as evaluating scholarship applications, summarizing or checking student work'; this concerns AI in decisions about people and checking student work, so P73 as the nearest type.
units.anchor: traditionally human activities such as evaluating scholarship applications, summarizing or checking student work
units.fit_note: Only says to be mindful and points to task-force recommendations; does not state that a human must decide.

units.why: States that 'these tools make mistakes. They can give wrong information, fake information'; accuracy warning, so P31, informs.
units.anchor: These tools make mistakes. They can give wrong information, fake information

units.why: 'you are just as responsible for the content of that work as if you had only used your brain' makes the user answerable for AI-assisted output, so P29, must, addressed to faculty users.
units.anchor: you are just as responsible for the content of that work
units.frag_end: used your brain to produce it.

units.why: 'It is a good idea to help graduate students be aware of these policies' on funders' and publishers' GAI rules in research; research and scholarship rules, so P62, should, addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: many granting agencies and publication venues have posted policies regarding permitted use of generative AI
units.frag_end: at the outset of a project.
units.fit_note: Also asks faculty to make graduate students aware of those policies.

units.why: The Center for Teaching and Learning 'has compiled information that instructors experimenting with GAI may find useful'; resource support for faculty, so P63, informs.
units.anchor: instructors experimenting with GAI may find useful

units.why: 'The Faculty Senate has ruled that the unauthorized use of GAI by students to complete coursework is in violation of the academic honesty policy' classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: unauthorized use of GAI by students to complete coursework is in violation of the

units.why: Says 'scholars should familiarize themselves with the GAI use and disclosure policies of publication venues'; a research rule that defers to venue rules, so P62, should.
units.anchor: scholars should familiarize themselves with the GAI use and disclosure policies of publication venues

units.why: Says 'in the right circumstance, faculty will want to explore its potential uses in teaching and learning' and calls GAI 'innovative and exciting'; names an opening for AI in teaching, so P87, informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI is innovative and exciting; in the right circumstance, faculty will want to explore

documents.title: Guidance on Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Undergraduate Student Success Center page answering whether students may use generative AI: not without instructor permission, and assume no if the instructor is silent. It also advises instructors on syllabus statements, wearable devices, and handling suspected AI misuse without relying on detectors.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Students cannot use Generative AI ... to complete any academic work without instructor permission' and 'should assume they are not allowed', which is a ban unless explicitly permitted.

units.why: 'Students cannot use Generative AI ... to complete any academic work without instructor permission' bans AI by default unless permitted, so P01 (default ban); the fallback sentence is coded separately as P06.
units.anchor: to complete any academic work without instructor permission.

units.why: 'If an instructor has not given explicit permission ... students should assume they are not allowed' states what applies when the syllabus is silent, so P06, not P01.
units.anchor: students should assume they are not allowed to do so

units.why: 'Students should always receive instructor permission to use Generative AI in any part of completing academic work' makes the instructor the one who grants use, so P04; it extends permission to any part of the work.
units.anchor: Students should always receive instructor permission to use Generative AI in any part
units.fit_note: Frames instructor decision as a permission students must obtain, for any part of the work.

units.why: 'Instructors should have clear expectations on Generative AI use in their courses, available to students in their course syllabus' asks for a syllabus statement, so P09.
units.anchor: Instructors should have clear expectations on Generative AI use in their courses

units.why: 'We also suggest instructors cover this policy in their courses at the beginning of the semester' asks instructors to talk about the policy in class, so P66 (explain and discuss), course-start.
units.anchor: cover this policy in their courses at the beginning of the semester
units.fit_note: Suggests covering the policy at semester start; does not say to give reasons.

units.why: 'consider including specific guidelines for different types of assignments' leaves the rule to be set per assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: consider including specific guidelines for different types of assignments

units.why: 'The policy states that students cannot use or attempt to use unauthorized materials including generative AI tools in any academic exercise without instructor permission' reports that the integrity policy classes unauthorized AI as a violation, so P36.
units.anchor: students cannot use or attempt to use unauthorized materials including generative AI tools

units.why: Says wearable devices 'with built-in video/audio recording capabilities and/or generative AI assistance ... may pose risks when it comes to securing assessments', which covers AI built into devices, so P07, informs.
units.anchor: wearable smart devices with built-in video/audio recording capabilities and/or generative AI assistance
units.fit_note: Concerns wearables such as watches and eyeglasses, not editors or IDEs.

units.why: 'Instructors should specify their expectations regarding use of wearable smart devices in their course syllabus' asks for a syllabus statement about AI-enabled devices, so P07.
units.anchor: Instructors should specify their expectations regarding use of wearable smart devices in their course syllabus.

units.why: 'Students should verify use of such devices is allowed prior to using them' tells students to check before using, so P10 rather than P07.
units.anchor: Students should verify use of such devices is allowed prior to using them.

units.why: 'the first step is to notify the student and request a meeting to discuss the situation' tells instructors to talk with the student before escalating, so P57.
units.anchor: the first step is to notify the student and request a meeting

units.why: 'AI detectors can produce false negatives and false positives' says detectors are unreliable, so P39, informs.
units.anchor: AI detectors can produce false negatives and false positives in their reporting.

units.why: 'The Academic Integrity Office does not recommend relying on detection tool reports when addressing suspected academic misconduct' advises against relying on detectors, so P39.
units.anchor: does not recommend relying on detection tool reports when addressing suspected academic misconduct

units.why: Says detector use 'may raise data and privacy concerns', a privacy risk of the tools, so P50, informs.
units.anchor: use of these tools may raise data and privacy concerns
units.fit_note: Concerns privacy risk of detectors rather than of generative AI tools.

units.why: 'we suggest that the instructor identify components of the student's work that raise concerns and ask the student to address those concerns directly in a conversation' replaces detector evidence with a conversation, so P57.
units.anchor: ask the student to address those concerns directly in a conversation

units.why: 'they should report the incident following the reporting procedures in the policy' is the formal reporting step if suspicion remains, so P81.
units.anchor: they should report the incident following the reporting procedures in the policy

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: Faculty Senate Academic Integrity Policy, a general policy with generative AI named in the definitions of cheating and plagiarism and in the instructor expectations. AI is unauthorized unless the instructor permits it, and the rest covers the reporting and student-rights process.
documents.stance_why: The cheating definition covers 'unauthorized materials, including generative AI tools ... (unless explicitly permitted by instructor)', so AI is banned unless the instructor permits it.

units.why: The cheating definition includes 'unauthorized materials, including generative AI tools ... (unless explicitly permitted by instructor)', so unauthorized AI is misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: unauthorized materials, including generative AI tools, assistance, collaboration, information, or study aids
units.fit_note: Also makes AI banned unless an instructor explicitly permits it.

units.why: The plagiarism definition says 'representing the words, ideas, art ... of another, including generative AI tools, as one's own work'; it treats passing off AI output as misconduct, P36 (P19 is a student rule, this defines the infraction).
units.anchor: representing the words, ideas, art, and/or creative works of another, including generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Defines passing off generative AI output as one's own as plagiarism; also close to P19.

units.why: 'Instructors are to be clear about the expectations in their course(s)/assignment(s)' requires instructors to state how work is to be completed, so P09.
units.anchor: Instructors are to be clear about the expectations in their course(s)/assignment(s)
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific here; the later instructor-expectations item names generative AI.

units.why: 'Will provide clear guidelines in syllabus and/or individual course assignments' with the examples including 'permission/restriction of generative AI tools' requires instructors to state AI rules, so P09.
units.anchor: permission/restriction of generative AI tools

units.why: 'Expectations within assignments may vary across courses; ... students should be familiar with individual course policies' makes students responsible for each course's rules, so P78.
units.anchor: students should be familiar with individual course policies

units.why: 'Instructors may analyze student work, electronically or by other means, for originality of content' allows tools to check originality, so P40.
units.anchor: Instructors may analyze student work, electronically or by other means, for originality of content.
units.fit_note: Not specific to AI; originality checking in general.

units.why: 'Any violation ... will result in negative consequences that may hinder an individual assignment grade, course grade, academic progress, or university enrollment' states general consequences in advance, so P37, though no specific penalty is set.
units.anchor: will result in negative consequences that may hinder an individual assignment grade, course grade
units.fit_note: Names kinds of consequence, not specific penalties.

units.why: 'Once an instructor suspects an academic integrity infraction, they are responsible for contacting the student(s) within 10 business days with a request to meet' sets the first step in a timed procedure, so P81 (P57 is the talk itself).
units.anchor: they are responsible for contacting the student(s) within
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; applies to every suspected infraction.

units.why: 'Will make a good-faith effort to communicate proactively with student(s) when an academic integrity infraction is suspected' tells instructors to talk to the student first, so P57.
units.anchor: Will make a good-faith effort to communicate proactively with student(s) when an academic integrity

units.why: 'Will not assign a grade on the basis of suspicion' sets an evidence standard, so P69.
units.anchor: Will not assign a grade on the basis of suspicion.

units.why: The students' rights list includes 'The opportunity to reject the informal process', so students may contest an allegation and ask for a hearing: P64.
units.anchor: The opportunity to reject the informal process

units.why: 'Upholding academic integrity is centralized in the Academic Integrity Office' names the office that owns and enforces the policy, so P80.
units.anchor: Upholding academic integrity is centralized in the Academic Integrity Office

units.why: 'Graduate TAs are responsible for reporting to the instructor of record any suspicions of academic dishonesty' tells TAs to report suspected misuse upward, so P81.
units.anchor: Graduate TAs are responsible for reporting to the instructor of record any suspicions

units.why: 'This resolution and any corresponding documentation must be filed with the Academic Integrity Office' requires filing informal resolutions with the office, so P81.
units.anchor: This resolution and any corresponding documentation must be filed with the Academic Integrity Office.

notes: Three university-layer documents coded. No school, computing or course documents collected. Senate policy is mostly general integrity process; only AI-relevant and AI-governing provisions coded.
